headline: Copper plunges to a seven-month low as rate-hike bets and the AI unwind hit metals
detail: On Nov 18, LME three-month copper closed down about 5.7% at $12,471/t and COMEX lost roughly 5.5% to about $5.65/lb, with zinc and tin also off about 5%. A strong dollar, near-certain Fed hike odds and fund selling are dragging copper scrap bids lower.

headline: Fed minutes show nearly all officials expect a December hike, and two floated a half point
detail: Minutes of the October meeting, released Nov 18, show broad support for a quarter-point hike in December, with core inflation running near 3.5% annualized. CME FedWatch put the odds near 95%. That keeps the dollar strong and weighs on all dollar-priced metals.

headline: U.S. ferrous scrap moves up while nonferrous slides
detail: For Nov 6–12, ScrapMonster had shredded auto scrap up $15/t and #1 busheling, #1 HMS and HMS 80/20 up $10/t, citing stronger mill buying, thin inbound flows and dealers holding material. That supports a firm December ferrous trade.

headline: Clean copper scrap down 27 cents a pound in three sessions
detail: On Nov 16, bare bright and #1 and #2 copper fell another 8¢/lb, a 27¢/lb drop over three sessions, while most aluminum and brass grades slipped 1¢ and steel held flat. Expect more copper scrap cuts after Nov 18's futures plunge.

headline: Nucor raises its hot-rolled coil price for an 18th straight week, to $1,310
detail: Nucor's weekly hot-rolled coil spot price rose $15 to $1,310 per short ton with 3–5 week lead times, and Kallanish puts U.S. HRC at $1,350–1,400. Strong sheet prices keep electric-arc mills hungry for prime scrap.

headline: Dollar index reaches its highest in nearly 20 months
detail: The dollar index hit about 103.4 on Nov 16 and pushed toward 104 after the hawkish minutes as markets priced a December hike and more in 2027. A stronger dollar makes metals costlier for overseas buyers and pressures export scrap.

headline: Dalian iron ore futures hit their lowest level since 2022
detail: On Nov 16, Dalian's most-traded iron ore contract fell 3.3% to 648 yuan/t, its lowest since November 2022, and Mysteel's 61% fines index fell to $88.05. Cheaper ore lowers costs for blast-furnace mills and can pull global steel prices down.

headline: China's October data miss again: factory output +4.8%, retail sales +0.4%
detail: Industrial output rose 4.8% year on year and retail sales only 0.4%, while fixed-asset and property investment fell sharply for January–October. Weaker Chinese demand is a key reason base metals are selling off.
source: National Bureau of Statistics of China

headline: Aluminum, nickel and tin fall along with copper
detail: By midday Nov 18, LME aluminum was down 2.2% at $2,869/t after a near one-year low the day before, nickel down 2.5% and tin down 7.1%; losses deepened into the close. Lower exchange prices feed through to aluminum scrap grades like UBC, 6063 and cast.

headline: October housing starts up 9.9%, but permits drop to their weakest in years
detail: Starts rose to a 1.309 million annual rate, but permits fell 7.4% to 1.295 million and single-family permits hit their lowest since January 2023. Falling permits point to softer demand for rebar and copper wire ahead.

headline: Platinum falls to a 14-month low and palladium to about $950
detail: Platinum dropped more than 3% on Nov 18 to its lowest since September 2025 and palladium fell about 2% to near $950/oz on the strong dollar and Fed outlook. Lower PGM prices cut what catalytic converters are worth to yards.

headline: Gold breaks below $3,800 and silver slides
detail: Gold fell about 2% to the high $3,700s, its lowest since September 2025, and silver lost 3–4% as FedWatch showed a December hike near 96% odds. This is a rates-and-dollar move rather than weaker physical demand.

headline: LME copper stocks pile up as prices slide
detail: LME copper inventories climbed to about 320,000 t by mid-November from an August low near 205,000 t, and COMEX broke below $6/lb on Nov 16. Rising visible stocks remove a key prop for prices.

headline: Banks warn a pullback in AI data-center financing could slow copper demand
detail: UBS and JPMorgan flagged that Nvidia may step back from financing AI data-center deals, which could delay builds that use a lot of copper. Goldman blamed the copper drop more on fund positioning than on weaker fundamentals.

headline: China's physical copper stays tight even as futures fall
detail: China's Yangshan copper import premium sat near record highs and Shanghai exchange copper stocks fell 18% in a week to near a three-year low. That tightness could limit how far copper falls once fund selling stops.

headline: China's October crude steel output falls to 70.8 Mt, lowest since December
detail: October output fell 3.8% from September and 1.6% from a year earlier, with January–October down 2.8%. Weaker Chinese steelmaking pulls down iron ore and global scrap demand.

headline: Nickel stuck near $16,000 as the market swings to surplus
detail: The International Nickel Study Group expects a 19,000-t surplus in 2026 widening to 70,000 t in 2027, with possible Indonesian ore-quota cuts the main support. That matters for stainless scrap prices.

headline: October existing-home sales fall to a 16-year low
detail: Sales fell 5.5% to a 3.75 million annual rate, the lowest since 2010, with mortgage rates above 7%. Weak housing turnover softens demand for appliance and building-material metals.

headline: Stellantis plans to sell its idled Brampton plant, putting 2,200 jobs at risk
detail: Stellantis plans to sell the Ontario plant, idled since 2023 for a paused electric-Jeep retool, as Ontario and Ottawa press the company ahead of a meeting with its CEO. It is another sign of North American EV capacity being pulled back.

headline: GM files notice of 506 layoffs at its Fairfax, Kansas, plant
detail: GM filed a WARN notice for 506 workers at Fairfax Assembly, which builds the Chevrolet Bolt and Equinox. Lower Midwest auto output means less prime busheling scrap coming off stamping plants.

headline: U.S.-Canada talks progressing, but no steel or aluminum tariff relief yet
detail: After a long call with Trump, Carney said the sides are making progress but are not there yet. Any deal easing steel and aluminum tariffs would hit Midwest aluminum premiums and cross-border scrap and steel flows.

headline: China's new home prices still falling, though more slowly
detail: October new home prices in 70 cities fell 2.4% from a year earlier, versus 2.8% in September. Property remains a drag on Chinese steel and copper demand.

headline: World Gold Council ties gold's slide to higher real yields and leveraged selling
detail: Ten-year TIPS yields rose about 30 bp in November and leveraged investors sold to raise cash, while central banks kept buying (321 t in Q3). That central-bank buying gives some support under the selloff.
